newsitem.title: UK: UK's Daily Telegraph February circulation falls.
newsitem.headline: UK's Daily Telegraph February circulation falls.

text.p: The Daily Telegraph, Britain's largest-circulating national newspaper, posted a 1.95 percent circulation drop in February from January, while the circulation of arch-rival the Times nudged ahead 0.12 percent, according to figures released Friday.

For the six-month period September 1996 to February 1997 the Times' circulation raced ahead 17.93 percent, while the Daily Telegraph posted a 5.56 percent gain, the Audit Bureau of Circulation (ABC) reported.

The ABC said the Daily Telegraph, part of Canada's Hollinger Inc, saw average daily circulation in February fall to 1,119,852 from 1,142,094 in January. Circulation of the Times, part of Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd empire, edged up to 767,809 from 766,922 in January.

For the six months ended February the Times had average daily circulation of 795,777 compared to 674,802 a year-earlier. The Daily Telegraph in the six months had circulation of 1,106,361, up from 1,048,053 in the year-earlier period.

The Sunday Times continued to hold a healthy lead in the Sunday market, rising 2.61 percent in February to 1,360,225 from 1,325,595 in January. The Sunday Telegraph fell back 0.81 percent in February to 889,803 from 897,025 in January.
For the six-month period The Sunday Telegraph jumped 25.48 percent to 835,635 in the prior-year period, while the Sunday Times gained 5.10 percent to 1,345,753 from 1,280,495.
Total circulation of Britain's five daily broadsheet newspapers fell 0.83 percent in February, while total circulation for the six months ended February rose 5.47 percent.

The Independent and its sister newspaper, the Independent on Sunday -- a joint venture of Mirror Group Newspapers Plc and Ireland's Independent Newspapers Plc -- posted sharp circulation losses for February and for the six months. The Independent fell 10.16 percent in the six months, although February circulation rose 1.53 percent over January. The Independent on Sunday lost 12.42 percent in the six months, while rising 3.38 percent in February over January, according to ABC figures.
